thread:
incident-bot: [PAGER] P1 - Elysium (enterprise tenant vpc-23) experiencing elevated 5xx rate and sustained tail latency in eu-west-2. Alerting on dedicated pool pool-d-42. Auto-escalation to on-call.

Emma Chen: Oncall ack — I'm looking. Seen reports from synthetic and customer telemetry (elen@elysium on live). Can someone grab initial impact? :eyes:

Raj Patel: I have the metrics up — 5xx spiked ~09:12 UTC, error budget burning on pool-d-42. Throughput is stable but a subset of hosts returning 503s. Might be a network/instance exhaustion or routing config.

Dan Morris: Logs show repeated KV cache misses + worker OOMs on a couple nodes. Stack traces attached to our log aggregator show the inference worker hitting accelerated kernel fallback.

Sylvia Park: Customer is in active session with CS. Julio is on the call. Julio, any customer-side notes?

Julio (CS): Confirmed — Elysium reports UI slow, some API calls timeout. They see requests routed to eu-west-2 only. They're asking for an ETA and whether we can shift traffic. I told them we're triaging and will propose mitigations.

Emma Chen: Short plan: 1) Isolate tenant from pool-d-42 hosts showing OOMs. 2) Shift a portion of traffic to eu-west-1 warm pool. 3) If stable, update DNS weights to move majority traffic. 4) Keep DNS TTL low during cutover.

Raj Patel: Agree. We should avoid a full DNS failover until warmness metrics (KV priming + latency) look good. We'll do staged weighted shift (25/50/75/100).

Dan Morris: Preparing route command. Using internal router tool 'rictl' — command for staged shift:

```
# stage 1: 25% to eu-west-1
rictl route traffic-shift --tenant elysium --from eu-west-2 --to eu-west-1 --percent 25 --policy weighted
# check priming and SLOs for 15m
```

Emma Chen: Before we run, confirm dedicated pool isolation strategy. We can either drain problematic nodes in pool-d-42 or attach a routing-filter to exclude malfunctioning hosts. Which is quicker?

Kai (Ops Lead): Filtering at the router layer is fastest (no instance reboots). Apply a routing filter for the tenant to exclude nodes with hostnames eu2-worker-03/07. Dan, can you craft the filter?

Dan Morris: Doing. Filter applied: `deny-host eu2-worker-03,eu2-worker-07 for tenant elysium` — applied to staging routing layer and now to prod. Observability shows those hosts out of rotation.

deploy-bot: Routing filter change deployed (id: rf-9923) by Dan. No errors.

Raj Patel: After filter, 5xx dropped ~40% within 2 minutes. Good sign. Ready to start traffic-shift.

Emma Chen: I'll run the 25% shift now. Monitoring: latency, 5xx, error budget, KV miss rate. All teams watch.

Dan Morris: Command executed.

```
rictl route traffic-shift --tenant elysium --from eu-west-2 --to eu-west-1 --percent 25 --strategy weighted --dry-run false
```

Sylvia Park: CS on call confirms customer sees partial improvement for some operations. They're still noticing sessions that hit eu-west-2 fail.

Raj Patel: Metrics: eu-west-1 latency baseline +20ms, 5xx near zero for shifted proportion. KV cache priming climbing as expected. Keep at 25% for 12 minutes to validate.

Emma Chen: Holding. If stable at T+12m, go to 50%. If regress, rollback to 0.

~12 minutes later~

Raj Patel: T+12m: metrics stable. No new OOMs, error rate for elysium overall dropped 62%. Proceed to 50%.

Dan Morris: Executed 50% step.

Emma Chen: Running. Also prepping DNS weight change plan with low TTL (60s) as fallback. DNS team, stand by to update weighted A records for elysium.example-cust.com if routing shift needs reinforcement.

Kai (Ops Lead): Remember: if we touch DNS, coordinate with customer and ensure their internal caches accept low TTL. Julio, can you confirm client-side TTL behavior?

Julio (CS): Confirmed with Elysium — they honor low TTL and can accept switching. They're asking for a timeline to minimize user disruption. I'll tell them staged plan and ETA ~30-45 min to full shift.

deploy-bot: Traffic shift to 50% completed.

Raj Patel: 50% steady for 10m. Some tail latency uplift (+12ms) but within SLO. We can move to 75% and prepare DNS as contingency.

Dan Morris: Also primed KV cache across warm fleet; cache hit rate now at ~82% for shifted requests. That should reduce per-request CPU.

Emma Chen: Initiating 75% now. Please keep hot metrics open and traces for last 1h.

Dan Morris: 75% in place. Monitoring...

Sylvia Park: Customer reports majority flows are now healthy. They want to know when we'll flip the primary routing.

Emma Chen: We'll wait until 100% shift is stable for 10 minutes, then we can consider making eu-west-1 the primary by changing DNS weights. Plan for DNS: set eu-west-1 weight 100, eu-west-2 weight 0, TTL 60s. Keep fallback routing rules in case of regression.

Raj Patel: Note: we should register a brief maintenance annotation in the tenant's audit logs and set postmortem owner. Dan — you ok for postmortem?

Dan Morris: Yep, I'll own the postmortem. I'll collect logs and kernel fallback traces.

~After further monitoring~

Raj Patel: 100% traffic now on eu-west-1. 5xxs trending to baseline. No new OOMs.

Emma Chen: Initiating DNS weight change as agreed. Julio, ping customer before we update DNS.

Julio (CS): Pinged customer — they consent.

Emma Chen: DNS change command (DNS team):

```
dnsctl set-weights elysium.example-cust.com --region eu-west-1=100 --region eu-west-2=0 --ttl 60
```

deploy-bot: DNS change queued and applied (chg-id dns-7782). Propagation observed.

Sylvia Park: Monitoring for cache-stale hits. Most clients re-resolve quickly due to low TTL. A few older middleboxes may still hit eu-west-2 for up to ~5m. Watch for errors.

Raj Patel: Observation: residual errors at the edge dropping to zero at T+4m. Good.

Kai (Ops Lead): Now that traffic is on eu-west-1, we should keep a warm pool in eu-west-2 for 24h and throttle new workloads there while we investigate root cause. Also start capture for a bucket of failed requests pre-cutover for triage.

Emma Chen: Agree. I'll set autoscale min for eu-west-2 dedicated pool to keep warm instances but prevent scale-up beyond baseline:

```
rictl pool set-scaling pool-d-42 --min-instances 2 --max-instances 6 --mode warm
```

Dan Morris: Collected crash dumps and will correlate with kernel fallback versions; initial hypothesis: a quantization kernel regression triggered under particular token lengths.

Raj Patel: Customer impact summary for CS and SRE leaders: ~15% of session requests errored at peak for ~18 minutes. Service restored to baseline after staged traffic shift + host exclusion. No data loss, but higher latency for some users during cutover.

Julio (CS): Customer notified with summary and timeline. They're appreciative of the staging and quick mitigation. Want a follow-up 1:1 tomorrow to review RCA.

Emma Chen: Postmortem owner: Dan Morris. Severity: P1 -> reduced to P2 after stable. Follow-up actions: 1) Patch quant kernel + test harness, 2) Improve routing filter automation, 3) Add a runbook for staged tenant traffic-shift with DNS fallback.

Kai (Ops Lead): Handoff: Emma remains on incident lead for next 30m then handoff to Raj for post-incident monitoring. Any objections?

Raj Patel: Ack. I'll take post-incident watch.

Emma Chen: Thanks all. Closing active mitigation. Will update thread with postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=stabilized, incident_id=INC-2026-ELY-4321, severity=P2, owner=Dan Morris.
